title: Nudge token-equality guard does not protect against dispatcher's prime-token side-channel
description: The up-front guard only compares `nudgePaymentToken` against the caller-supplied `paymentToken` argument. The actual ERC20 the dispatcher pulls is determined inside `nftMinter.mint(...)` — V2's mint resolves the prime token from the dispatcher's own configuration, not from the `paymentToken` argument. The argument is just the token this helper uses to fund the mint via approval. If the caller passes a `paymentToken` that does NOT match the dispatcher's prime token (a misconfiguration, or an exploit), the inner mint will pull a DIFFERENT token from BatchNFTMinter via the max approval. If that prime token happens to coincide with `nudgePaymentToken`, the dispatcher will pull from the nudge stash to pay for mints, and the guard does not catch this case because it only checks `paymentToken` argument. The contract's NatSpec at lines 84-88 acknowledges that a dispatcher/paymentToken mismatch causes the inner mint to revert — but that revert path assumes the BatchNFTMinter has not approved the prime token. With the nudge token sitting in the contract and approved indirectly via `forceApprove(nftMinter, max)` on a DIFFERENT token... wait, the approval is on `paymentToken`, not on `nudgePaymentToken`, so the dispatcher cannot pull the nudge token. RE-EVALUATION: the dispatcher uses `safeTransferFrom(BatchNFTMinter, ...)` on the prime token, which requires an allowance on the prime token. The approval is only on `paymentToken`, so prime-token != paymentToken does cause a revert (no allowance), as documented. THIS FINDING IS A FALSE POSITIVE on the direct path. The residual concern is that if the nftMinter contract ever changes its mint() to accept the prime-token allowance from msg.sender (the BatchNFTMinter) on a DIFFERENT erc20 it already happens to hold, the guard would not protect — but that requires nftMinter behavioural change and is not a bug in BatchNFTMinter today.
exploit_scenario: Marked as informational — the direct exploit does not work because approvals are scoped to `paymentToken` only. Documenting for completeness in case the dispatcher/minter contract evolves to query token approvals indirectly.
recommended_mitigation: Demote to defensive: also revert if `nudgePaymentToken == address(nftMinter)`. Optionally, after the loop and before the nudge transfer, assert that the contract's `nudgePaymentToken` balance has not changed compared to a snapshot taken before the mint loop — this would catch any future dispatcher behavior that reaches into other tokens.
notes: Initially flagged as medium based on the prompt's question about NFT-supply token side; on detailed analysis the approval scoping closes the direct attack. Keeping as informational/QA-grade.
